newsitem.title: USA: Station seeks to have top casino in K.C..
newsitem.headline: Station seeks to have top casino in K.C..

text.p: Station Casinos Inc opens its newest casino in Kansas City tonight with an eye on being the top operator in what analysts consider one of the tightest gambling markets in the United States.

At a cost of $255 million, Station Casinos Kansas City Hotel & Casino boasts a 200-room hotel and the fourth largest casino in the U.S. Some financial analysts, however, have questioned the wisdom of building such a large operation there. Two recent openings have not met initial expectations and the market, although growing, is still considered small.

In an interview with Reuters, Station Chief Financial Officer Glenn Christianson acknowledged the controversy over its entry into Kansas City and he pegged it as one reason Station's stock has languished around nine recently.
He noted Kansas City overall generated about $350 million in casino revenue in 1996, up from about $260 million in 1995.

"One thing we know is the size of a market is a function of the size and quality of (casino) projects in that market," Christianson said. "We are going to expand the market...and I think we'll be able to attract people from much farther distances as a tourist destination."
Much of Station Kansas City's success will depend on whether or not its size and diverse entertainment venues can attract not only gamblers, but weekend partiers, too.

Station Kansas City's 3,000 slot machines are 62 percent over the 1,848 of its largest competitor, Harrah Entertainment Inc's North Kansas City casino. Its 190 table games are about 52 percent above Harrah's 125, according to recent research from Salomon Brothers.
In Missouri, gamblers must wait for casinos to open new gambling sessions every two hours.
Station Kansas City can cut the wait down to 15 minutes from what has been as much as one hour and 45 minutes in some places, Christianson said.
Moreover, a 1,400-seat arena, 12 restaurants and 11 should attract more people than just gamblers.
Analysts believe Station Kansas City can generate cash flow between $30 million and $55 million in 1997.
Christianson noted that the wide range in estimates stems from market uncertainty.
He said the company will release its fourth quarter earnings on February 4 and will discuss initial results at Station Casinos Kansas City at that time.
He declined to comment on analysts's consensus forecast the company will earn $0.21 a share in the fourth quarter.
